coverage_note: § 18 (the universal synthesis of transcendental time) and § 36 (egological-temporal coexistence and succession). §§ 12 and 15 and the four other sections with term hits are not extracted.

units.claim: Identification is met first as an all-pervasive passively proceeding synthesis in the form of continuous inner time-consciousness, every experience having its experience-temporality.
units.quote: It confronts us first as an all-pervasive, passively proceeding synthesis in the form of the continuous inner time-consciousness. Every experience has its experience-temporality.

units.claim: The objective temporality that appears is to be distinguished from the inner temporality of the appearing, which streams along in phases that are changing appearances of the same object.
units.quote: we must distinguish the objective temporality that appears — e.g., that of this cube — from the inner temporality of the appearing (e.g., of the cube-perceiving)

units.claim: All-encompassing inner time-consciousness is called the fundamental form of the universal synthesis that makes all other syntheses possible, its correlate being immanent temporality itself.
units.quote: The fundamental form of this universal synthesis, which makes all other syntheses of consciousness possible, is the all-encompassing inner time-consciousness. Its correlate is immanent temporality itself

units.claim: All experiences of the ego found in reflection must present themselves as temporally ordered within the constant infinite horizon of immanent time.
units.quote: according to which all experiences of the ego, reflectively found, must present themselves as temporally ordered — as temporally beginning and ending, as simultaneous and successive — within the constant infinite horizon of immanent time

units.claim: Essential laws of egological-temporal coexistence and succession are said to govern compossibility, everything emerging in the ego having its temporality and partaking in the form-system of universal temporality.
units.quote: Essential laws of egological-temporal coexistence and succession govern. Whatever emerges in my ego — in intentional experiences, in constituted unities, in ego-habitualities — has its temporality and partakes in the form-system of universal temporality.
